thread:
Ana: Quick sync — we need to finalize how the model capability discovery endpoint handles edge cases for launch. Customers keep asking about tool-level granularity, streaming support flags, and per-model token ceilings. What do we accept for MVP vs. follow-up?

Mohit: For MVP I'd push a conservative surface: list supported capability groups (chat, embeddings, rerank, tools, streaming) + a per-capability boolean. Avoid per-tool exhaustiveness initially.

Lee: +1. If we expose every tool name we end up chasing house-keeping. But teams building tool-routing need a stable signal. Propose two levels: capability_group and capability_detail (optional string) — detail can be an opaque tag for now.

Sara: From customers: 1) Compliance teams need explicit streaming: true/false, and max_stream_window_tokens. 2) Integrators want a tools list for function-calling routing (they may restrict allowed tool ids). Can we support an allowlist blob for Dedicated/Private only?

Mohit: We can do a minimal allowlist field, but mark it only populated for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can return "tools_supported": ["limited"] or null. Also call out that tool names are not stable API contracts unless we version them.

Jen: Security note: if we return tool metadata (endpoints/scopes) we should strip internal URIs and not leak infra details. Any allowlist must be adoptable with org-level scoping. Also need KMS/consent annotation for models that process PII from tools.

Lee: Token limits: let's return two values: "soft_token_limit" (preferred scheduling limit) and "hard_token_limit" (rejects if exceeded). Helps SDKs pick safe defaults. Defaults vary by model size; runtime can fill these.

Ana: Can someone sketch the proposed response shape (compact) so we can include it in the spec doc? Will use for prioritization checklist.

Mohit: Here's a rough draft — we can iterate:
```
{
  "model": "redwood-v1",
  "capabilities": {
    "chat": true,
    "embeddings": true,
    "rerank": false,
    "tools": true,
    "streaming": true
  },
  "tools_allowlist": ["payments:charge", "crm:lookup"],
  "capability_details": {
    "tools": "catalog-v1",
    "streaming": "full"
  },
  "soft_token_limit": 4096,
  "hard_token_limit": 8192
}
```
(Notes: tools_allowlist only populated for Dedicated/Private; hosted returns empty array or null.)

Sara: That shape looks actionable. Can we add a small field for "fallback_model" when a capability is partial? e.g., rerank: false -> fallback_model: "rerank-lite" so customers can implement graceful degradation.

Mohit: ok to add fallback_model as optional string. Runtime will populate based on routing policies.

Jen: Add a "compliance_tags" array for region/sensitivity that can inform data handling: e.g., ["eu-pii"] — also optional and only set when necessary.

Ana: Launch criteria proposal (short): 1) Hosted returns stable shape for all curated models; 2) Dedicated/Private supports tools_allowlist + org scoping; 3) Streaming flag accurate + soft/hard token limits applied; 4) Security sign-off on leakage and compliance_tags. If any item is missing we mark for beta on enterprise tier.

Lee: Implementation risks: kernel/runtime may not know accurate hard limit until runtime mem check. We'll fallback to conservative defaults per instance class. Call out that token limits are best-effort and may vary by sequence length.

Sara: From CS: prioritize allowing integrators to query capabilities programmatically. If we delay tools list, they'll build brittle heuristics. Suggest exposing allowed_tools_count and an opt-in detailed_tools endpoint for customers on enterprise terms.

Ana: OK action items — Mohit to update shape with fallback_model + compliance_tags, Lee to add token-limit caveat text, Jen to draft security checklist, Sara to confirm top 5 enterprise customers who want detailed_tools endpoint. We'll aim to include this in the roadmap doc for the next planning cycle.
